what: An endless WebGL strip of vertical photo cells (217:269), each one-third of the screen height — it follows wheel and drag by .085 per Frame for a sticky flow (wheel 1x · touch 1.6x), and the cell crossing the 39% line from the top of the screen becomes the current cell and fires fx:active (used to change the left title). The cell under the hand becomes current first with a hand cursor, and pressing fires fx:select (if blocked, the consumer handles the navigation) and then goes to that cell’s address. Locked cells (data-locked) get a shader gaussian blur of .5. At first the cells rise from .9 screen height below, upper cells first at a .08s stagger over 1.65s, and only the cell caught on the top edge falls from .83 height above. The shader is precompiled at setup.

options.[data-fx-part=item]: Slot — data-label (photo description) · data-src (photo if present) · href or data-href · data-locked (blurred locked slot)
options.vh: Cell height (ratio of screen height), default 1/3
options.title: Row currently selecting the cell (ratio from the top of the screen), default .39
options.trigger: Band phase line (rain from top of screen), default .3
options.center: CSS selector for the element to use as the band’s horizontal center (like the Work text in the menu) — if none, the panel center
options.min: At or below this width (px) skip the canvas and leave the cell list as is, default 768

use:
Work name…
— Load three (window.THREE) first. On the panel, fx:active {index} Takes it and changes the title
note: The original gives each cell a photo texture. With no photo, a gray plate labeled with data-label is drawn on a 2D canvas and used as the texture (change the colors with --fx-strip-fill, --fx-strip-line, --fx-strip-ink). The wheel is received across the whole window, so use it on a page where the strip covers the screen (Work list).
